purpose: Bus-configurable watchdog timer: once enabled it counts prescaled clock ticks and pulls the system reset rstn_o low when the count reaches the configured timeout without a password-checked feed, or (in strict mode) on an illegal access; a sticky lock freezes the configuration and a reset-cause register records why the last reset happened.

conceptual_assets.name: watchdog configuration (enable, timeout, strict)

C.why: Read back to any bus reader at L109-113; enable, strict and timeout are not secrets and no line keeps them secret.

I.why: Writes at L94-97 happen only while ctrl.lock=0 (L93). Clearing enable holds cnt at 0 (L131) and blocks both resets (L155, L156); changing timeout moves the reset point (L144).

A.why: A small ctrl.timeout makes cnt = ctrl.timeout early (L144) and rstn_o asserts (L155, L161) again and again: a reset storm. enable=0 removes the reset service entirely (L155).

U.why: The lock takes effect only if enable is already 1 (L95 uses the current ctrl.enable), so one write of enable+lock leaves it unlocked; strict=0 (L156) makes locked-write attempts harmless no-ops; L91-97 have no privilege condition (bus_req_i.priv has no local use).

conceptual_assets.attack_effect: Clearing ctrl.enable at L94 while unlocked holds cnt at 0 (L131-132) and keeps hw_rst_timeout low (L155), so a hung or hijacked CPU is never reset; setting ctrl.timeout low at L97 makes L144/L161 reset the system repeatedly.

conceptual_assets.name: configuration lock (ctrl.lock)

C.why: Read back at L110; the lock state is not a secret.

I.why: ctrl.lock gates every control write (L93). Its only software write (L95) sits inside the lock=0 branch, and only rstn_sys_i clears it (L76), so it is sticky.

A.why: Setting or clearing the lock does not block delivery of any value; its effect is on the integrity of the control word.

U.why: The lock is ANDed with the current ctrl.enable (L95): it cannot be set in the same write that enables the watchdog.

conceptual_assets.attack_effect: If ctrl.lock were cleared, L93 would reopen L94-97 to writes, so the configuration attacks above become possible after software believes the watchdog is locked.

conceptual_assets.name: watchdog count and timeout decision (cnt, cnt_timeout)

C.why: cnt is not exported (no CARRIES edge to any port); disclosure has no stated harm.

I.why: cnt is cleared only when enable=0 or reset_wdt=1 (L131-132) and advances only on cnt_inc (L133-134); any other clear or hold keeps cnt below ctrl.timeout, so L144 never fires.

A.why: cnt advances only on prsc_tick (L129-130), which comes from clkgen_i (L141); if the tick is blocked, the timeout decision is never produced.

U.why: cnt_started (L130) delays counting until the first tick after enable; this is a start condition, not a defeat.

conceptual_assets.attack_effect: Holding cnt below ctrl.timeout keeps cnt_timeout at 0 (L144), so hw_rst_timeout (L155) and rstn_o (L161) never assert.

conceptual_assets.name: feed authorization (password-checked restart)

C.why: The password is a fixed source constant (L35) compared at L102 and never stored in an element or exported; the module has no line that protects its secrecy.

I.why: Only an exact 32-bit match asserts reset_wdt (L102-103); any other value sets reset_force (L105). Forging reset_wdt clears cnt at L131-132.

A.why: The feed path is not gated by ctrl.lock (L101-103), so feeding stays possible when locked; no line blocks it.

U.why: With ctrl.strict=0 a wrong password (L105) sets reset_force, but hw_rst_access needs strict (L156), so guessing has no consequence.

conceptual_assets.attack_effect: Asserting reset_wdt (L103) without the password clears cnt (L132) each time, so a runaway program keeps the system alive and the watchdog never resets it.

conceptual_assets.name: hardware reset request (timeout and access violation)
conceptual_assets.flow: timeout -> system reset / access violation -> system reset

C.why: The reset request is a control action, not data to hide.

I.why: rstn_o is the OR of hw_rst_timeout and hw_rst_access (L161); a spurious request resets the SoC, a suppressed one removes recovery. reset_force (L99, L105) is the violation decision feeding L156.

A.why: Delivery of the recovery reset depends on ctrl.enable and prsc_tick (L155); in strict mode any bus master can force a reset by a bad write (L99/L105 -> L156 -> L161).

U.why: strict=0 disables the access-violation reset (L156); enable=0 disables both (L155, L156).

conceptual_assets.attack_effect: A deliberate wrong-password write in strict mode forces hw_rst_access (L156) and resets the whole system on demand; suppressing hw_rst_timeout (L155) removes the watchdog's recovery.

conceptual_assets.name: reset cause record (reset_cause)

C.why: Readable by any bus reader (L111); the cause code is not a secret.

I.why: Only hardware conditions write it (L169-176); no bus write path exists; it is reset only by rstn_ext_i (L168), so it survives the watchdog's own system reset and tells software why the reset happened.

A.why: Read back unconditionally on any read (L108-111).

U.why: rstn_dbg_i low has top priority (L171-172) and records "01", overriding a coincident "10" or "11".

conceptual_assets.attack_effect: Driving rstn_dbg_i low after a violation-triggered reset replaces "11" with "01" (L171-176), so software reading L111 sees a debug reset instead of an access violation or timeout.

hypotheses: No privilege or debug-mode check on configuration, feed or read-back: bus_req_i.priv and bus_req_i.debug occur only at L24. Whether the bus fabric filters user-mode accesses is outside this source.
rstn_o probably drives the system reset that returns as rstn_sys_i; if so, a watchdog reset also clears ctrl.lock (L76) and ctrl.enable (L75). Not visible here.
The feed password (reset_pwd_c, L35) is a fixed constant in the source; it guards against accidental feeding by runaway code, not against an informed attacker.
Availability of the tick depends on an external clock generator honouring clkgen_en_o (L140) and delivering clkgen_i (L141).
Violations are never signalled on the bus: bus_rsp_o.err is constant '0' (L84); software learns of them only through reset_cause after the reset.
Recording the cause at L173-176 assumes clk_i keeps running while rstn_o is asserted; the outside clock and reset wiring decides this.

map_assessment.used_for: Indexing every occurrence and edge; tracing the enable, lock, timeout, password and reset paths; confirming reset_cause has no bus write path; confirming ctrl.lock's only software write sits inside its own lock=0 branch; confirming the lock is cleared only by rstn_sys_i and reset_cause only by rstn_ext_i; confirming bus_req_i.priv/debug have no local use; confirming the read path is not gated by bus_req_i.addr.
map_assessment.insufficient_for: The password constant (constants are not elements, so the L102 edge shows only bus_req_i.data GATES reset_wdt, not what it is compared with); the if/elsif priority in reset_identifier (GATED_BY edges do not show that rstn_dbg_i wins); that L95 uses the old registered ctrl.enable; the meaning of the cause codes; the outside wiring of rstn_o, clkgen_en_o and clkgen_i. All of these came from reading the source.
map_assessment.errors_found: None on the edges checked. Classification notes only: bus_req_i.data at L95 is typed GATES (single-bit AND operand) although it is also the data value of ctrl.lock; the ctrl aggregate has storage 'not assigned' and no relationships while its fields are 'edge'.

process_notes: 1) Read the prompt and the whole source (it is small). 2) Indexed the map with a script into a per-element listing of occurrences and relationships. 3) Wrote the use-case flows from the ports and processes: configure, lock, feed, count, timeout reset, access-violation reset, cause recording, read-back. 4) Traced each flow on map edges and confirmed each edge on its line. 5) Answered C/I/A/U per value with a mechanism line. 6) Assigned roles, then applied the exclusions. Where the map changed a decision: the absence of any bus edge into reset_cause and its RESET_BY rstn_ext_i (not rstn_sys_i) made its integrity answer yes; the declaration-only occurrences of bus_req_i.priv/debug moved the missing privilege check into U and the hypotheses; rstn_dbg_i's edge is GATES (not RESETS), so it was treated as a data condition (sets) rather than excluded as a reset. Source reading was needed for the password compare, the if/elsif priority, and the old-enable semantics of L95. Every cited occurrence id was checked against its line by script.
